scope: Asking-price regression on one local snapshot after price-text redaction, exact deduplication and conservative property-group holdout; no production model was overwritten.

dataset.target_kind: listing asking price, not verified transaction price

split.test_usage: one-time diagnostic comparison across four fixed models; not used for fitting, tuning or production deployment selection

method.target_transform: log1p before fit, expm1 after prediction for every model

conclusion: XGBoost is numerically best on all four reported test metrics in this diagnostic, but the test comparison is not a production model-selection protocol and does not establish generalization.

raw_metadata_correction.obsolete_runtime_wording: test groups are isolated and never used for model selection
raw_metadata_correction.correct_interpretation: The test groups were isolated from fitting and tuning, but their scores were used for the one-time four-model diagnostic comparison. No production model was selected or deployed.
raw_metadata_correction.reason_not_rewritten: The raw artifact is retained byte-for-byte so its recorded SHA-256 remains verifiable.

limitations: The property entity key is a conservative location/physical-attribute heuristic for legacy rows without durable property IDs; it can merge distinct similar properties or miss relistings with changed metadata.
One fixed holdout, no cross-validation, confidence interval or independent temporal/source dataset.
The target is asking price and the snapshot is not evidence of verified transaction-value accuracy.
The historical legacy scores are not directly comparable because their random split retained target-text and duplicate leakage.
